0.
0.1 This

FOREWORD

Indian Standard ( Part III ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 21 July 1982, after the draft finalized by the Optical and Mathematical Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council.

0.2 Fast development in the field of instruments has brought a significant It has been felt over the years change in their basic content and design. that IS : 2352-1963* does not cater for the present day needs of the instrument and is also not in line with the recent trends in climatic and environmental testing procedures to be adopted for improving their quality and rehability. It has, therefore, become necessary to have uniform and more rational testing procedures as far as possible. This series of standards on climatic and durability tests ( IS : 10236 ) has been prepared with this objective. 0.2.1 It is proposed to withdraw the existing Indian ( IS : 2352- 1963* ) as soon as the tests mentioned therein are the new series ( IS : 10236 ). 0.3 This standard deals with cold tests temperature use and storage, with or without applicable both thermal shock. 7.1 Method
7.1.1 The condition.

instrument

shall be subjected

unpacked

NOTE - If it is expected that ingress of condensed moisture may have deleterious effect in the movement of moving parts, the instrument shall be kept enclosed in a polythene bag having an appropriate qnantity of active silicagel.

7.1.2 At the laboratory temperature the instrument under test shall be The temperature of the chamber shall introduced into the chamber. then be lowered to the specified severity or any other severity as specified in the relevant instrument specification at a rate not exceeding 5�C per 5 minutes.
7.1.3 On attaining the temperature equilibrium if required by the relevant instrument specification, the electrical/electronic arrangement fitted in the instrument shall be switched on from outside to check whether it is functioning or not. After this verification the arrangement shall be switched off. 7.1.4 After attaining the temperature equilibrium the instrument shall remain at the low temperature appropriate to the severity for 4 hours or such other period as may be specified in the relevant instrument specification. 7.1.5 At the end of the period of exposure, if required by the relevant instrument specification the electrical/electronic arrangement fitted in the instrument shall be switched on from outside and its functioning seen. 7.1.6 At the end of the test, the chamber shall be switched off and allowed to rise to the temperature as specified in the standard atmospheric conditions for recovery. 5

7.2.2 At the laboratory temperature the instrument under test shall be introduced into the chamber. The temperature of the chamber shall then be lowered to the specified severity or any other severity as specified in the relevant instrument specification at a rate not exceeding 5�C per 5 minutes.
7.2.3 After temperature equilibrium has been attained, the instrument shall remain at the low temperature appropriate to the severity for 16 hours or such other period as may be specified in the relevant instrument specification. 7.2.4 After that period the chamber shall be switched off and allowed to rise to the temperature as specified in the standard atmospheric conditions for recovery. shall be removed from the chamber 7.2.5 Recovery - The instrumemt and any droplets of water adhering to the instrument shall be removed The instrument shall then be kept at standard atmospheric by shaking. conditions for recovery for not less than one hour nor more than two, hours. 7.3 Method III Test with thermal shah shock for low temperature use.

IS : 10236 ( Part III ) - 1982 7.3.3 On attaining the temperature equilibrium if required by the relevant instrument specification, the electrical/electronic arrangement fitted in the instrument shall be switched on from outside to check whether it is functioning or not. After this verification the arrangement shall be switched off.
7.3.4 After attaining the temperature equilibrium the instrument shall remain at the low temperaturfor 4 hours, a ppropriate to the severity or such orther period as may be specified in the relevant instrument specification. 7.3.5 At the end of the period of exposure if required by the relevant instrument specification the electrical/electronic arrangement fitted in the instrument shall be switched on from outside and its functioning seen. 7.3.6 The instrument shall then be removed from the chamber and if required by the relevant instrument specification its moving parts shall be examined at a temperature near to the specified severity in open or covered condition.
NOTE When operated at the low temperature, normally some stiffness in movements may be expected but with this stiffness it sh.41 be possible to set the instrument at any desired position with ease at that low temperature.

7.3.7 Recovery - After the above examination, if for moisture protection polythene bag has been used, the instrument shall be taken out .of the bag and kept at the standard atmospheric conditions for recovery for not less than one hour nor more than two hours. Any droplets adhering to the instrument shall be removed by shaking. After this the instrument shall remain under standard atmospheric conditions for recovery for a further period of not less than one hour nor more than two hours.
